question: Did the Partner channel's share of completed orders go up from 2024 to 2025? If it did, give Partner's 2025 completed orders by region. If it did not, give the 2025 completed orders by region for whichever channel's share rose the most.
plan: The answer depends on a condition: evaluate the condition first with its own query, then answer only the branch that applies.

sql_attempts.sql: WITH channel_shares AS (SELECT o.channel, SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND o.order_date <= '2024-12-31' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_2024, SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date <= '2025-12-31' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_2025, SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND o.order_date <= '2024-12-31' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND order_date <= '2024-12-31') AS share_2024, SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date <= '2025-12-31' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND order_date <= '2025-12-31') AS share_2025 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.channel), partner_diff AS (SELECT share_2025 - share_2024 AS diff FROM channel_shares WHERE channel = 'Partner'), target_channel AS (SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT diff FROM partner_diff) > 0 THEN 'Partner' ELSE (SELECT channel FROM (SELECT channel, share_2025 - share_2024 AS diff FROM channel_shares ORDER BY diff DESC LIMIT 1)) END AS chosen_channel) SELECT r.region_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders_2025 FROM regions AS r JOIN customers AS c ON c.region_id = r.region_id JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id CROSS JOIN target_channel WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.channel = target_channel.chosen_channel AND o.order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date <= '2025-12-31' GROUP BY r.region_name ORDER BY completed_orders_2025 DESC
